CVE-2026-40913.description: Apache Airflow's public Import Errors API returns the raw parse-failure stack trace to any user with the `ImportError.can_read` permission when the failing file has no registered DAG. This happens when a file fails to parse before any DAG is defined, or when all of its previously registered DAGs are removed but the parse error remains. Users who should not see that file's details can read stack traces that may expose file paths and code. Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later, which restricts these stack traces to users with the new `IMPORT_ERRORS_ALL` permission.

CVE-2026-50204.description: Apache Airflow's audit log stored Connection and Variable secret values in cleartext in the `Log.extra` column because the secrets masker matched only on configured sensitive key names. An authenticated low-privilege user with read access to the event-log / audit API — with no prior access to the affected connection or variable — could read those rows and recover the credentials verbatim. Users should upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later, which masks these values and restricts the affected audit rows to authorized users. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.

CVE-2026-54863.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Mamunur Rashid Review Schema review-schema allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects Review Schema: from n/a through 3.1.4.

CVE-2026-66675.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in StylemixThemes Motors motors-car-dealership-classified-listings allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Motors: from n/a through 1.4.128.

CVE-2026-68982.description: Apache Airflow's CeleryExecutor ran callback workloads (`ExecuteCallback`, used for deadline-alert callbacks) without validating the workload's authentication token. Anyone able to write to the Celery broker could enqueue a forged callback and execute arbitrary code on every CeleryExecutor worker, without Airflow credentials. Deployments using the CeleryExecutor are affected. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later, in which the worker claims the callback through the Execution API, validating the token, before running it.

CVE-2026-76185.description: Apache Airflow's Task SDK secret cache built its keys from the team name and secret id with unescaped `_` delimiters, so different (team, secret id) pairs could collide. In multi-team deployments a Dag author could read another team's Variable or Connection value by crafting a colliding secret id. Only deployments with both `core.multi_team = True` and `secrets.use_cache = True` are affected. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later. Deployments that cannot upgrade can set `secrets.use_cache = False`.

CVE-2026-82337.description: Apache Airflow rebuilt deadline alert fields through generic deserialization, which imports and instantiates the class named in the serialized Dag, in the scheduler and API server. A Dag author could cause classes within Airflow's deserialization allow list to be constructed in those processes with arguments they control. Deployments whose Dags use deadline alerts are affected. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-45360, which only hardened the `reference` field; deployments that applied that fix remain affected through the `callback` and `interval` fields. Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to 3.4.0 or later.

CVE-2026-82436.description: Description `DefaultStateSerializer`, used to persist and restore stateful bolt checkpoints, configured Kryo with class registration disabled and an instantiation strategy that constructs objects without invoking their constructors, then deserialized whatever bytes the state store returned. A party able to write to the topology's keyspace in the state store, for example a co-tenant of a shared Redis instance or anyone with network access to it, could therefore place a serialized object graph that executes code inside the worker JVM when the state is restored. This requires the Redis-backed state provider, which is not the default. Write access to a state-store key is a data-plane privilege; code execution in the worker JVM is not, so the two are not equivalent. Mitigation Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the state serializer requires registered classes. Note that this is a behaviour change for existing state: checkpoints written by an affected version may fail to restore, and a migration step may be required. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict network and credential access to the state store to the cluster itself. Credit The ASF -- found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache Storm.

CVE-2026-82440.description: Description Nimbus instantiates the class named by a topology's `topology.scheduler.strategy` when scheduling it. The allowlist intended to constrain that choice, `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist`, was treated as "allow any class" when unset, and it had no entry in the shipped `defaults.yaml`, so unset was the shipped state. An authenticated submitter could therefore cause Nimbus to instantiate any class on the Nimbus classpath that has a no-argument constructor. Storm's own production artifacts contain classes with side effects suitable for this: instantiating `org.apache.storm.testing.InProcessZookeeper` starts a ZooKeeper server with its own threads and sockets and nothing closes it, and `org.apache.storm.LocalCluster` behaves similarly. Repeated submissions therefore consume threads, sockets and memory in the most privileged daemon in the cluster. Mitigation Upgrade to 3.1.0, where an unset allowlist means the strategies shipped with Storm rather than any class. Note that this is a behaviour change: a cluster running an out-of-tree scheduler strategy without an explicit allowlist will have those topologies refused until the class is added to `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist`. The rejection message names the refused class and the configuration key. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist` explicitly to the strategies they intend to permit.

CVE-2026-86468.description: Apache Airflow's CLI records its arguments in the audit log but masks secrets by argument position, so some supported command shapes leave secrets in cleartext, for example a trailing `--description` on Variable commands, `--conn-extra`, and the inline `--password` of `airflow keycloak-auth-manager` commands. A user who can read audit events but is denied Variable and Connection access can retrieve those values through the event-log API. Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to 3.4.0 or later. Audit-log entries written before the upgrade keep the cleartext values: purge the affected entries and rotate the secrets they contain. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.

CVE-2026-86829.description: Apache Airflow's scheduler fully deserializes XCom values written by task code while evaluating task dependencies. A Dag author, who controls what a task writes to XCom, therefore controls data that is deserialized inside the scheduler process - a context the Airflow security model reserves for code installed by the Deployment Manager, above the worker-scoped execution capability a Dag author is documented to have. Deployments that treat Dag authors as less trusted than Deployment Managers are affected, and the scheduler must be evaluating a task dependency that reads a task-written XCom value. Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to version 3.4.0 or later, which restricts dependency evaluation to primitive XCom values.

CVE-2026-92683.description: Incorrect authorization in the @authentication directive JWT where filter evaluation in Neo4j @neo4j/graphql versions 7.0.0 before 7.6.7 allows an attacker holding an otherwise-valid JWT to bypass all but the first filter condition via a multi-condition jwt where filter written in generic operator syntax.

CVE-2026-96285.description: Apache Airflow 3.3.1 shipped a fix for CVE-2026-67260 that checks the scheduler's decoded `next_kwargs` value is a dictionary, but performs that check only after deserializing the whole stored payload. Deserialization reconstructs nested objects of classes permitted by the deserialization allow-list — which by default includes Airflow's own classes — and runs their constructors inside the scheduler process before the check can reject the value. A Dag author, who controls a task's `next_kwargs` through the task execution API, can therefore still trigger constructor execution in the scheduler when the `awaiting_input` timeout sweep processes the task, and in the API server when the task instance is served to a worker using an older Execution API version; no non-default configuration is required. Versions before 3.3.0 are not affected. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-67260: deployments that upgraded to 3.3.1 for that issue must also upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.

CVE-2026-106008.description: The FraudLabs Pro SMS Verification WordPress plugin from 1.11.2 to 1.12.1 does not perform authorisation or validity checks before marking a WooCommerce order's SMS verification as completed, allowing unauthenticated users to forge the verified state of an order and bypass the plugin's SMS verification control.

CVE-2026-106466.description: The JWT Auth WordPress plugin through 3.0.2 does not invalidate previously issued refresh tokens when a user changes or resets their password or removes a connected device, allowing an attacker who obtained a refresh token before such an event to keep issuing valid access tokens and retain authenticated access to the account, up to Administrator.

CVE-2026-113702.description: A security flaw has been discovered in iomad up to 4.5.15/5.0.11/5.1.8/5.2.4. Affected by this vulnerability is the function local_iomad_pluginfile in the library public/local/iomad/lib.php of the component PDF Certificate Handler. The manipulation results in authorization bypass. The attack can be launched remotely. The patch is identified as ac7427130865ce0ed80870813317c87ae3060fa4/7bf0b10199782e04aa579e9d516e473b164afd1c/db903abdcb3aba124cce670608ae6d7ba5f51a84/66f7417c5357b7575e39e8be390602156c1a1225. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

CVE-2026-115252.description: The Confection WordPress Cable WordPress plugin from 0.4.0 to 0.4.7 does not perform any capability or nonce checks before saving its settings and writing one of them, unmodified, into a standalone PHP file that it then serves, allowing unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.

CVE-2026-118196.description: OAuth 1 rebinding vulnerability in Apache Allura. This issue affects Apache Allura: through 1.22.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.22.1, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-119515.description: Missing Authorization vulnerability in Mamunur Rashid Radius Booking — Booking Calendar for Appointments & Services radius-booking allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Radius Booking — Booking Calendar for Appointments & Services: from n/a through 1.0.20.

CVE-2026-120367.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. The JSON message builders, including the Gson, Moshi and HTTP/2 variants, buffered the entire request body with no size limit, so an unauthenticated caller could exhaust server memory with a large JSON request. Version 2.0.2 bounds JSON request bodies with the configurable jsonMaxRequestSize parameter. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-120761.description: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. When a client built an AxisService from a WSDL URL, through ServiceClient or AxisService.createClientSideAxisService, wsdl4j import resolution was enabled and the documents named by wsdl:import and xsd:import were parsed by wsdl4j's own XML parser, which processes DOCTYPE declarations and external entities. An attacker who controls a WSDL, or a document it imports, could therefore read local files or make the JVM issue network requests. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-120832.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. When Axis2 built a service description from a WSDL, through ServiceClient, AxisService.createClientSideAxisService or WSDLToAxisServiceBuilder, it fetched the absolute URLs in wsdl:import locations and in xsd:import and xsd:include schemaLocations with no scheme or host restriction; the AAR and WAR deployment resolvers also passed absolute schema locations on to the network. An attacker who controls a WSDL or schema processed by an Axis2 application could therefore make the JVM send requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-123753.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. An unauthenticated caller could supply a non-anonymous WS-Addressing wsa:ReplyTo or wsa:FaultTo address, and Axis2 would open a connection to that address to deliver the response or fault, allowing requests to internal hosts and delivery of response content to a host of the caller's choosing. From 2.0.2, decoupled responses are refused unless allowNonAnonymousResponseEndpoints is enabled, and enabled endpoints are restricted by scheme and screened at both the header-parsing and transport-selection layers. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-123766.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting) vulnerability in the OpenAPI module of Apache Axis2/Java. The Swagger UI page served by the OpenAPI module wrote a value derived from the request's Host header into the page without encoding, allowing script injection in the context of the Axis2 origin. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-123770.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. The multipart/form-data and application/x-www-form-urlencoded message builders read the request body directly from the transport stream with no size limit, so the servlet container's post-size limit did not apply, and multipart temporary files were not deleted. An unauthenticated caller could exhaust memory or disk. Version 2.0.2 bounds these bodies with configurable limits and deletes temporary files. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-123779.description: Direct Request ('Forced Browsing') vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. The exposeServiceMetadata service parameter was enforced only on the ?wsdl, ?wsdl2 and ?xsd queries. For a service that had disabled it, the packaged .wsdl and .xsd file routes, the named-WSDL ?wsdl=NAME route of the standalone HTTP server, the OpenAPI, Swagger UI and MCP catalog endpoints, the services listing, WS-MetadataExchange GetMetadata and the ping module still disclosed its metadata to anonymous callers, including operation names and request and response schemas. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

The manipulation of the argument userName/userPwd/userEmail/userId leads to improper authorization. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product uses a rolling release model to deliver continuous updates. As a result, specific version information for affected or updated releases is not available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-124621.description: A vulnerability was determined in kongxin-github Java_Library_Management_System up to 70a6eb6b96fe64575d8051f1a59055bfc5dc5885. This affects the function UpdateAdmin.deleteuser/UpdateAdmin.updateadmin/UpdateAdmin.updatepass/Book.addbook/Book.modifybook/Book.deletebook/Category.addcategory/Category.setcategory/Landing.sureadmin of the file src/view/MainInterface.java of the component Swing UI Layer. This manipulation causes improper authorization. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. This product follows a rolling release approach for continuous delivery, so version details for affected or updated releases are not provided. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-112172.description: CGM XDent and XMedical expose PHP synchronization endpoints that allow unauthenticated attackers to manipulate session variables and execute arbitrary SQL queries against backend MySQL databases.

CVE-2026-118450.description: Venere is installed outside Program Files and loads/registers unsigned components from locations where an unprivileged user may create files.

CVE-2026-118458.description: The shared AIS login routing selects a production-shipped test DAO and plaintext comparison for the H and V application codes, accepting fixed administrator accounts.

CVE-2026-118459.description: A time-derived emergency password can be derived from publicly available application code, enabling authentication without legitimate credentials.

CVE-2026-118460.description: Embedded private keys protected by a shared password can be used to sign practitioner assertions for arbitrary practitioner identifiers, enabling unauthorized practitioner token requests.

CVE-2026-118461.description: The shared client accepts caller-controlled doctor identifiers for read and write operations without requiring authentication or authorization credentials.

CVE-2026-118462.description: Update components download and execute code without proper authenticity verification, relying on ignored hashes or forgeable checksums. Some update paths also permit archive traversal or script execution.

CVE-2026-118464.description: Shared cryptographic services use fixed vendor-wide secrets, deterministic IVs, null salts, and reversible transformations to protect credentials, IPC data, configuration values, and clinical fields.

CVE-2026-118465.description: Shared components expose hard-coded Access, workgroup, CCBasic, DBISAM, and related database credentials that are identical across installations.

CVE-2026-118467.description: Shared telemetry and logging components store or transmit patient and doctor identifiers, clinical information, and low-entropy identifiers without adequate pseudonymization or protection.

CVE-2026-118468.description: XML parsers process attacker-influenced update manifests or network responses with external entity resolution enabled, potentially allowing XML External Entity (XXE) attacks.

CVE-2026-121629.description: A flaw was found in GStreamer's adaptive streaming demuxers (HLS, DASH, MSS). When processing a media playlist or manifest, URIs referenced in the manifest content are fetched without restricting which URI schemes are permitted. An attacker who controls a manifest URL, or who can inject content into an HTTP manifest response, can include file:// URIs pointing to arbitrary local files, causing the affected application to read and process those files. In automated or server-side deployments such as media recorders, proxies, and downloaders, this can lead to disclosure of sensitive local files. Existence of files can also be inferred through differing error responses even when content is not directly observable.

CVE-2026-124684.description: This issue can cause a heap-use-after-free when an embedder unloads a ReloadableString buffer while a previously returned raw character pointer remains in use. Successful triggering may cause the Escargot-based process to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

CVE-2026-110468.description: WidzialniCMS is vulnerable to Unrestricted File Upload in the /panel/controllers/save_photo.php endpoint. Due to a client-controlled permission check parameter and insufficient validation of the currentpath parameter, an unauthenticated attacker can upload arbitrary files to any locations on the server, leading to Remote Code Execution. This issue has been fixed in version 2.5.

CVE-2026-110469.description: WidzialniCMS is vulnerable to Unrestricted File Upload in the /panel/upload.php endpoint. Due to a client-controlled permission check parameter and insufficient validation of the uploadPath parameter, an unauthenticated attacker can upload arbitrary files to any locations on the server, leading to Remote Code Execution. This issue has been fixed in version 2.5.

CVE-2026-112168.description: The Magistra software uses weak custom encryption, relies on an outdated compression algorithm to protect the database, and contains embedded secrets.

CVE-2026-112169.description: Magistra software contains undocumented backdoor functionality that allows authentication bypass and the creation of a privileged user account without credential verification.

CVE-2026-112170.description: The software downloads upgrade files without performing integrity checks, allowing the installation of tampered updates.

CVE-2026-112171.description: An attacker can inject malicious SQL statements through user-controlled input, allowing unauthorized access to, modification of, or disclosure of database data.

CVE-2026-112204.description: WidzialniCMS is vulnerable to Reflected XSS in the /index.php endpoint. An attacker can prepare an URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser, allowing e.g session cookie theft. This issue has been fixed in version 2.5.

CVE-2026-112205.description: WidzialniCMS is vulnerable to Bruteforce Protection Bypass in the login functionality. The cookie-based lockout can be bypassed by omitting the login_count and login_timeout cookies, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to perform an unlimited number of login attempts. This issue has been fixed in version 2.5.

CVE-2026-118790.description: Multiple hardcoded credentials are embedded within product components and administrative functionalities. These credentials may enable unauthorized access to privileged accounts, services, or application features across affected deployments.

CVE-2026-118791.description: The application implements software update functionality without adequate authenticity and integrity validation, allowing update packages to be accepted without sufficient cryptographic verification.

CVE-2026-118792.description: Default credentials permit access through AcuXDBC.

CVE-2026-118795.description: Administrative roles and module permissions are stored in mutable local database fields, allowing privilege escalation for attackers with database write access.

CVE-2026-118798.description: Multiple sensitive authentication data, including credentials, OAuth-related secrets, session information, and authentication artifacts, are exposed through application logs and persistent client-side storage, enabling unauthorized access and session compromise.

CVE-2026-119610.description: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good, specifically in the H.264 RTP depayloader element. When processing MTAP16 or MTAP24 multi-time aggregation RTP packets, a signed/unsigned integer conversion error causes the remaining-length counter to underflow to a large positive value when the packet is truncated. This allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds heap read of up to approximately 64 KiB of process memory by sending a single malformed RTP packet. Successful exploitation can crash the receiving GStreamer pipeline (denial of service), and in relay or transcoding deployments where output is accessible to the attacker, may expose adjacent heap contents.

CVE-2026-119613.description: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in ash-project ash_ai allows a caller of an AshAi tool to read internal error details, including module names and data values, by making a tool call fail. AshAi.ToToolError gained an implementation for Ash.Error.Unknown.UnknownError that returns the error's error field as is, and AshAi.Tool.Errors.format/1 sends that text to MCP clients (tool calls and resource reads in AshAi.Mcp.Server) and to the model in AshAi.ToolLoop. Ash stores the full Exception.format/2 output of a raised exception, or inspect/1 of a bare {:error, term} return, in that field. A tool result that cannot be JSON-encoded raises a Protocol.UndefinedError whose text includes the inspected value, which can be a whole record with fields the tool never returns. None of these errors were logged. The fix logs them under an error id and returns only that id to the caller. This issue affects ash_ai: from 1.5.0 before 1.5.1.

CVE-2026-120854.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in iubenda iubenda iubenda-cookie-law-solution allows HTTP DoS.This issue affects iubenda: from n/a through 3.13.6.

CVE-2026-120856.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Rymera Web Co Invoice Gateway for WooCommerce – Invoice Payment Gateway invoice-gateway-for-woocommerce allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects Invoice Gateway for WooCommerce – Invoice Payment Gateway: from n/a through 1.1.6.

CVE-2026-121601.description: A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer plugin (gst-plugins-bad). When processing a specially crafted MXF media file, the demuxer indexes its internal delta-entry and slice-offset tables using values from the file without validating that they are within the bounds of the allocated arrays. A local attacker who tricks a user into opening a malicious MXF file can cause the application to crash (denial of service) and may be able to read limited amounts of heap memory adjacent to the affected arrays.

CVE-2026-121611.description: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-bad package. A use of uninitialized memory vulnerability exists in the H.265 (HEVC) bitstream parser when processing Video Parameter Sets that declare more than one HRD (Hypothetical Reference Decoder) parameter set. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a crafted H.265 media file or stream that, when processed by an application using GStreamer, causes unpredictable parser behavior and may crash the application. This can lead to a denial of service for any application using GStreamer to play back H.265 content.

CVE-2026-122673.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Wpmet ShopEngine shopengine allows Stored XSS.This issue affects ShopEngine: from n/a through 4.9.8.

CVE-2026-124079.description: rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.19 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.1 contain a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows unauthenticated network attackers to execute arbitrary code by pushing a crafted serialized job onto the Redis-backed Laravel Horizon queue, which runs without authentication in affected deployments. Laravel's CallQueuedHandler unserializes the job without class restrictions, allowing attackers to instantiate the existing App\\Jobs\\TaskDownloadRun class and invoke an attacker-controlled Artisan command. Attackers can leverage the bundled laravel/tinker package to execute arbitrary PHP and operating system commands as the queue worker's user, write a persistent web shell into the web-served storage/app/public directory, and read database credentials, stored device credentials, and API tokens. Where Redis is not directly reachable, authenticated attackers can deliver the payload through the application by configuring a device target that points at the rConfig server's loopback address.

CVE-2026-124622.description: A vulnerability was identified in olivier-ls PHP-FTS up to 1.1.3. This impacts the function TrigramIndex::open of the file Storage.php. Such manipulation leads to time-of-check time-of-use. The attack needs to be performed locally. Upgrading to version 1.1.4 will fix this issue. The name of the patch is 0b2fae333d6b022da7ed4c43e2d41aa03f91dff3. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The project maintainer explains: "[T]he attack requires write access to the index directory by a user other than the one running the application. That is a real shared-hosting scenario and worth defending against, which is why it is fixed but it is a hardening measure rather than a remotely reachable vulnerability, and the "Code Execution" impact additionally assumes the symlink target is a web-served .php file."

CVE-2026-124623.description: A security flaw has been discovered in PipraPay 3.0.0. Affected is the function system-settings-import of the file /sumo166/CVE-apply/blob/main/PipraPay/PipraPay/system-settings-import of the component ZIP Archive Handler. Performing a manipulation results in unrestricted upload. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-94434.description: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('OS command injection') vulnerability in TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Software Technologies Research Institute Pardus Boot Repair allows OS Command Injection. This issue affects Pardus Boot Repair: from 1.0.8 before 1.0.9.

CVE-2026-95648.description: Improperly controlled modification of Dynamically-Determined object attributes vulnerability in C-Prot Inc. C-Prot AppDefense allows Privilege Escalation. This issue affects C-Prot AppDefense: before 1.0.2729.

CVE-2026-119274.description: Infoblox NIOS version upto 9.1.0 contain a vulnerability related to improper input validation that allows a stored XSS

CVE-2026-119743.description: pdfmake before 0.3.14 contains a shared resource caching vulnerability that allows attackers to access cross-document cached resources by exploiting a process-wide virtual file system keyed only by URL without request headers or per-document access enforcement. Attackers can retrieve resources fetched with another caller's credentials or from URLs that a later document's access policy would deny, resulting in cross-document information disclosure and bypass of the URL access policy.

CVE-2026-121841.description: Other issue in Firefox for iOS. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox for iOS 160.0.

CVE-2026-121842.description: Privilege escalation in the Reader View component in Firefox for iOS. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox for iOS 160.0.

CVE-2026-121843.description: Privilege escalation in Firefox for iOS. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox for iOS 160.0.

CVE-2026-124624.description: A weakness has been identified in PipraPay 3.0.0. Affected by this vulnerability is the function hash_hmac of the file pp-content/pp-include/pp-adapter.php of the component pp-token anti-CSRF Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to hard-coded credentials. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-124625.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in PipraPay 3.0.0. Affected by this issue is the function deleteData of the file pp-content/pp-include/pp-functions.php of the component Admin Panel. The manipulation of the argument selected_ids/ItemID leads to sql injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-124635.description: A vulnerability was identified in kevquirk PureBlog up to 3.7.2. Impacted is an unknown function of the file admin/upload-image.php of the component Admin Image Upload Endpoint. Such manipulation leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 3.7.3 is recommended to address this issue. The name of the patch is 71f5b0de2ecb2bb2934048ed40e1155c107484e3. You should upgrade the affected component. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

CVE-2026-16283.description: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('OS command injection') vulnerability in Osbil Technology Ltd.Osbil Technology Ltd. OPanel allows OS Command Injection. This issue affects oPanel: before 1.20.66.

CVE-2026-95778.description: A remote code execution vulnerability exists in HPE Morpheus Software.

CVE-2026-95779.description: An exposure of the appliance’s confidential certificate information vulnerability exists in HPE Morpheus manager software.

545eeb4a7a4b2ddaeac615ed.title_ko: 구글, AI 코딩 오류 예방 위한 '코끼리-금붕어' 모델 플러그인 공개
545eeb4a7a4b2ddaeac615ed.summary_ko: 구글이 AI 코딩 에이전트의 설계 검토 과정을 개선하기 위한 오픈소스 플러그인 '코끼리-금붕어 모델(EGM)'을 공개했다. 프로젝트 전체 맥락을 기억하는 '코끼리'와 독립적으로 설계를 검토하는 '금붕어' 에이전트를 결합해, 코드 구현 전 발생할 수 있는 설계 오류를 최소화하도록 설계되었다.

b63c8a6e1a52c91a9b5f1461.title_ko: 대만 해커, AI 에이전트 활용해 타이베이 긴급 출동 기록 탈취
b63c8a6e1a52c91a9b5f1461.summary_ko: 대만의 한 공격자가 안전장치가 제거된 AI 모델 기반의 에이전트들을 이용해 대만 내 긴급 서비스 데이터 및 의료 정보를 탈취한 사례가 확인되었다. 공격자는 주로 보안이 취약한 API와 데이터베이스를 대상으로 했으며, 상용 AI 모델의 거부 정책을 우회하기 위해 로컬 환경에서 실행되는 모델을 사용했다.

a5d975da50e51b75da2492ab.title_ko: AI 사전 학습 데이터 0.1%만 오염시켜도 에이전트 백도어 생성 가능
a5d975da50e51b75da2492ab.summary_ko: AI 사전 학습 데이터의 일부만 조작하는 것만으로도, 이후 개발된 AI 에이전트에 원격 코드 실행 백도어를 심을 수 있다는 연구 결과가 발표되었다. 정상적인 미세조정 과정을 거쳐도 백도어가 제거되지 않았으며, 모델 규모가 클수록 공격 성공률이 높아지는 것으로 나타났다.

curation.reason_ko: AI 학습 데이터 0.1% 오염만으로 AI 에이전트에 원격 코드 실행 백도어를 심을 수 있음이 확인됨.

a67baf4e244a01fb4b38c5cd.title_ko: 구글 딥마인드, AI 에이전트 활용해 1024비트 RSA 암호 해독 비용 절감
a67baf4e244a01fb4b38c5cd.summary_ko: 구글 딥마인드와 연구진이 AI 에이전트를 활용해 노후화된 1024비트 RSA 암호 체계에 대한 공격 비용을 대폭 낮추는 방법을 발견했다. 이번 연구는 기존 암호화 체계에 대한 고정관념을 테스트한 결과로, 현대 표준인 2048비트 이상의 암호화 체계는 여전히 안전하다고 강조했다.

c45607788230df0792bfc2aa.title_ko: 모티프, 엔비디아 투자 유치...차세대 LLM '모티프 4' 개발 착수
c45607788230df0792bfc2aa.summary_ko: 모티프테크놀로지스가 엔비디아 등으로부터 투자를 유치해 차세대 파운데이션 LLM '모티프 4' 개발에 착수했다. 내년 1분기 공개 예정인 이 모델은 이전 모델의 성능을 넘어 상업성과 사용성을 극대화하는 방향으로 추진된다.

ecb8b922a05a74463d0c909e.title_ko: 누스 리서치, 오픈 모델의 정치적 편향성 완화한 '아레테-27B' 공개
ecb8b922a05a74463d0c909e.summary_ko: 누스 리서치가 알리바바의 큐원 기반 모델에 지도 미세조정을 적용해 정치적 편향성을 개선한 '아레테-27B'를 공개했다. 특정 국가의 선전성 답변 비율을 22%에서 0.9%로 낮추면서도 모델의 기존 코딩 및 에이전트 성능을 유지한 점이 특징이다.

734bce3bae3841d23ed0b490.title_ko: 개인정보보호위원회-KCPO, 2026 개인정보정책포럼 개최…AI 시대 예방적 보안 체계 논의
734bce3bae3841d23ed0b490.summary_ko: 개인정보보호위원회와 한국개인정보보호책임자협의회가 '2026 개인정보정책포럼'을 열고 AI 기반 해킹 위협에 대응하는 예방 중심의 개인정보 보호 체계와 책임경영 강화 방안을 논의했다. 정부는 예방적 보안 투자에 대한 인센티브 제공 등 규제 합리화를 추진하며, 전문가들은 기업 경영진이 외부 노출 자산 관리 등 선제적 보안 거버넌스를 갖추는 것이 중요하다고 강조했다.

3bf4c28c8ff5e89fb5c2d8d5.title_ko: LG유플러스, 서울대·KAIST·연세대와 한국어 특화 음성 AI 기술 개발 착수
3bf4c28c8ff5e89fb5c2d8d5.summary_ko: LG유플러스가 서울대, KAIST, 연세대와 'K-보이스 AI 얼라이언스'를 출범하고 차세대 음성 대 음성(V2V) 기술 기반의 'K-보이스 엔진'을 공동 개발한다. 이번 협력을 통해 말투와 맥락을 이해하고 대화의 흐름을 기억하는 자연스러운 한국어 음성 AI를 구현하여, 향후 자사 AI 서비스에 단계적으로 적용할 계획이다.

c3828f1b737cef92e3f3b0ee.title_ko: 아마존, 차세대 가정용 로봇 개발 재도전…'피지컬 AI' 기술로 실용화 모색
c3828f1b737cef92e3f3b0ee.summary_ko: 아마존이 과거 가정용 로봇 '아스트로'의 실패를 딛고 차세대 로봇 개발을 위한 조직을 재편했다. 환경을 직접 이해하고 행동하는 '피지컬 AI' 기술의 발전으로 가사 지원 및 일상 상호작용이 가능한 로봇의 실용 가능성이 높아짐에 따라, 아마존은 휴머노이드 로봇 스타트업 인수 등을 통해 가정용 로봇 시장에 다시 도전한다.

7ae879c167fab515f6d3047e.title_ko: AI 에이전트에 직급 부여하는 'AI 네이티브 조직' 확산
7ae879c167fab515f6d3047e.summary_ko: 국내 AI 기업들이 AI 에이전트에게 직급과 업무를 부여하고, 사내 해커톤 등을 통해 전사적인 AI 내재화를 추진하는 'AI 네이티브 조직'으로 진화하고 있다. AI가 단순 반복 업무를 수행하고 구성원은 AI 오케스트레이터를 관리하며 기획과 전략적 의사결정에 집중하는 업무 구조로의 전환이 본격화되는 추세다.

95a62c0771fd241d17995746.title_ko: 삼성-현대차, 미래 모빌리티 및 피지컬 AI 협력 강화

0ac1a0adf6cef34add163270.title_original: I Don't Care How You Hide It, I Care What You Do: Runtime Detection of Malicious ML Models
0ac1a0adf6cef34add163270.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-trained machine learning (ML) models shared through public platforms can be weaponized to execute malicious payloads during loading or inference. Existing scanners prove inadequate for detecting malicious models as they rely on static analysis and function denylists, support limited serialization formats, and miss attacks that replace denylisted functions with equivalent alternatives, exploit unsupported loading paths, or abuse legitimate framework APIs. To address this problem, we present ModelShield, the first runtime behavioral detection system for malicious ML models that attributes observed system-level behavior to specific model operations. It combines application-level instrumentation of ML framework APIs with eBPF-based syscall tracing, tracking model behavior across spawned threads and processes to separate model-triggered activity from environment noise. Attributed syscall sequences are classified using 195 detection patterns mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. We implemented ModelShield to support 17 ML frameworks and 36 formats. On an independent dataset, it is the only evaluated tool to achieve zero false positives, with false negatives limited to payloads that produce no malicious runtime behavior. It detected all 29 published evasion variants spanning function substitution, loading-path obfuscation, and TensorFlow API abuse, where no existing scanner achieved complete coverage. CVE-2026-123800.description: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 6.0.0 until 6.0.24, 7.0.23, 8.0.7, 9.0.6, 9.1.6, 9.2.7, 9.3.5, 10.0.8, 10.1.9, 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, Multitenancy.checkPermissionsForCreateOrUpdate in src/main/java/io/supertokens/multitenancy/Multitenancy.java does not adequately authorize updates to a parent connection URI domain or the base tenant. In a licensed multi-tenant deployment with multiple applications under one non-default connection URI domain and separate api_keys, an attacker holding one application's valid API key can update the parent domain because the CUD-target branch checks the domain without requiring the source application and tenant to be public. Because api_keys is not protected, the attacker can replace the parent key and then sibling application keys, read or modify sibling users, obtain sessions as those users, establish persistence through a sibling dashboard user, and lock out the sibling application's own key. In the advisory's v2 create or update handlers, omitting the optional identifier produces a base-tenant target that skips the permission branches and enterprise-feature gate, allowing changes to firstFactors, required secondary factors, and recipe-enabled flags that affect login integrity and availability. The base-target variant still rejects coreConfig and does not establish key theft. This issue is fixed in versions 6.0.24, 7.0.23, 8.0.7, 9.0.6, 9.1.6, 9.2.7, 9.3.5, 10.0.8, 10.1.9, 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.
CVE-2026-123800.summary_ko: SuperTokens Core의 멀티테넌시 권한 검사 미흡으로, 인증된 공격자가 다른 애플리케이션의 도메인 설정이나 권한을 수정하고 세션을 탈취하거나 서비스 가용성을 방해할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: SuperTokens Core의 멀티테넌시 권한 검사 미흡으로 인증된 공격자가 애플리케이션 설정을 수정하고 권한을 탈취할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-123270.description: Redpanda Connect versions 4.39 to 4.110 contain a missing authentication vulnerability that enables unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). In streams mode, the management HTTP API is exposed on `0.0.0.0:4195`, but authentication is disabled by default and there is no authentication gate protecting the stream CRUD routes. An unauthenticated attacker with network access to TCP/4195 can `POST` a malicious pipeline definition to `/streams/{id}` that includes code-executing processors such as `command`, `subprocess`, `ffi`, or unsafe `sql_raw`, thereby achieving arbitrary RCE on the host with the permissions of the Redpanda Connect service account. Because pipelines can also return command output in-band via HTTP, this vulnerability enables full host compromise, credential theft, and data exfiltration with no user interaction or credentials required. Starting with v4.111, the API endpoint was reconfigured as opt-in, so this and later versions are no longer vulnerable by default. However, RCE remains achievable on v4.111 and later if the management API is manually enabled via the `--bind-http` flag.
CVE-2026-123270.summary_ko: Redpanda Connect의 관리 HTTP API에 인증 누락 취약점이 존재하여, 네트워크 접근 권한이 있는 공격자가 임의의 파이프라인을 게시해 호스트 시스템에서 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Redpanda Connect의 관리 API 인증 누락으로 원격 공격자가 임의 코드를 실행하여 호스트를 완전히 장악할 위험이 있습니다.

CVE-2026-115934.description: An unauthenticated SQL injection can occur on the front end of any site that uses craft.search to perform a search, allowing stacked query execution and enabling escalation to an administrator. Note that this only affects MySQL/MariaDB. Impact * SQL injection — The attribute parameter is concatenated into the query unsanitized, and because PDO runs with emulated prepares, stacked statements execute. This gives unauthenticated read and write access to the application database. * Privilege escalation to administrator — The write primitive was used to set the admin flag on user ID 1 in the users table, confirmed by reading the value back. Craft short-circuits its permission checks on this single column, so no further changes were needed. The same primitive can overwrite any account’s password hash. Update to the patched versions (4.18.9 and 5.11.2) to get the fix. If you cannot update immediately, you can block front-end requests with %5Battribute%5D and [attribute] anywhere in the query string as a temporary mitigation.
CVE-2026-115934.summary_ko: Craft CMS에서 craft.search를 이용한 검색 시 MySQL/MariaDB 환경에서 SQL 인젝션이 발생할 수 있습니다. 이를 통해 공격자가 관리자 계정 권한을 탈취하거나 데이터베이스를 조작할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Craft CMS의 검색 기능에서 SQL 인젝션이 발생하여 관리자 계정 권한 탈취 및 데이터베이스 조작이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-109795.description: SAP NetWeaver does not perform necessary authorization checks and lacks sufficient input validation in certain remote-enabled functionality. An attacker with low privileges could send specially crafted input through a remote interface to inject and execute arbitrary code within the affected system. Successful exploitation could extend the attacker's reach beyond the vulnerable component, resulting in a high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability.
CVE-2026-109795.summary_ko: SAP NetWeaver의 특정 원격 기능에서 권한 확인 및 입력 검증이 부족합니다. 인증되지 않은 공격자가 원격 인터페이스를 통해 임의 코드를 삽입하고 실행하여 시스템 기밀성, 무결성, 가용성에 큰 피해를 줄 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: SAP NetWeaver의 원격 기능 내 권한 및 입력 검증 미흡으로 공격자가 시스템 내 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-125370.description: Kubero 3.0.0 through 3.1.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to forge administrative JWTs by using a hardcoded fallback signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset. Attackers can sign tokens with arbitrary role, userGroups and permissions claims, which JwtStrategy.validate() trusts without a database lookup, to take control of pipelines, applications, users and API tokens.
CVE-2026-125370.summary_ko: Kubero에서 JWT_SECRET이 설정되지 않을 경우 하드코딩된 기본 비밀값을 사용합니다. 공격자는 이를 이용해 관리자 권한을 가진 JWT를 위조하여 파이프라인과 애플리케이션 등을 통제할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Kubero에서 기본 JWT 비밀키 설정 누락으로 인증 우회 및 관리자 권한을 가진 토큰 위조가 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-121686.description: FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) is vulnerable to unauthenticated, remote code execution via MQTT. A firmware method accepts arbitrary shell commands delivered via Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) messages and executes them as root. Access is gated only by shared Internet of Things (IoT) credentials, with no per‑device authentication, enabling remote code execution as root across the fleet.
CVE-2026-121686.summary_ko: FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ 펌웨어의 MQTT 메시지 처리 과정에서 인증되지 않은 원격 코드 실행 취약점이 발견되었으며, 공유 IoT 자격 증명만으로 루트 권한의 명령 실행이 가능합니다.

curation.reason_ko: FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ 펌웨어의 MQTT 메시지 처리 취약점으로 공유 자격 증명만으로 루트 권한 명령 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-123807.description: Signal K Server is a server application that runs on a central hub in a boat. From 2.0.0 until 2.34.0 for Signal K Server and from 1.0.0 until 1.5.3 for @signalk/resources-provider, the v2 REST route GET /signalk/v2/api/resources/:resourceType/:resourceId accepts an unsafe resourceId that can escape the intended resource directory. The route passes the attacker-controlled resourceId through src/api/resources/index.ts to FileStore.getResource() in packages/resources-provider-plugin/src/filestorage.ts without adequate path containment, allowing arbitrary JSON files reachable by the server to be read. Related PUT and DELETE resource operations can write or delete files outside the storage root. Deployments with allow_readonly enabled permit anonymous reads, while other deployments require a readonly user token. Reading security.json exposes the HS256 JWT signing secret and password hashes, allowing an attacker to forge an administrator token. Administrative access to POST /skServer/providers can then create an Execute provider that runs commands with the server process privileges and persists its configuration across restarts. This issue is fixed in Signal K Server 2.34.0 and @signalk/resources-provider 1.5.3.
CVE-2026-123807.summary_ko: Signal K Server 및 관련 리소스 제공자에서 경로 제한 미흡으로 임의 파일 읽기, 쓰기 및 삭제가 가능합니다. 이를 악용해 보안 설정 파일을 노출하고 관리자 토큰을 위조하여 시스템 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Signal K Server의 경로 제한 미흡으로 임의 파일 조작 및 보안 설정 탈취, 관리자 토큰 위조가 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-125383.description: INDOTALENT WHMS (Asp.Net-Core-Inventory-Order-Management-System) before 10.20261109 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability caused by a hard-coded JWT signing key, issuer and audience in appsettings.json. Unauthenticated remote attackers can forge tokens for any user ID and role that the Tokens/DI.cs validator trusts, gaining administrator access to the entire API.
CVE-2026-125383.summary_ko: INDOTALENT WHMS에서 JWT 서명 키와 설정값이 하드코딩되어 인증 우회 취약점이 발생합니다. 원격 공격자가 임의 사용자와 역할에 대한 토큰을 위조하여 API에 대한 관리자 권한을 획득할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: INDOTALENT WHMS의 하드코딩된 JWT 서명키로 인증 우회 및 관리자 권한 획득이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-119756.description: Tasmota through 16.0.0, fixed in commit e97e1e4, contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in SendReceiveDeviceGroupMessage() that allows unauthenticated attackers on the local network to corrupt heap memory by sending crafted Device Groups messages over UDP port 4447 that cause the log_remaining counter to go negative and writes to exceed the fixed 512-byte buffer. Attackers can exploit this flaw to crash the device or potentially achieve native code execution on ESP8266 and ESP32 platforms that lack ASLR and heap cookies.
CVE-2026-119756.summary_ko: Tasmota의 SendReceiveDeviceGroupMessage() 함수에 힙 범위를 벗어난 쓰기 취약점이 존재하여, 로컬 네트워크의 공격자가 메모리를 손상시키고 장치를 충돌시키거나 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Tasmota의 SendReceiveDeviceGroupMessage() 함수 내 힙 범위를 벗어난 쓰기로 인해 원격 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-124001.description: NASA JPL ION-DTN 2.2.1b through 4.2.0 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the Datagram Retransmission (DGR) convergence layer that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a maliciously crafted 64-bit svcDataLength value that wraps a 32-bit allocation size calculation. Attackers can exploit the dgr_receive API's unchecked memcpy operation using synthetic datagrams or DGR traffic over internal IPC or custom transports to trigger an out-of-bounds write, leading to denial of service or potential remote code execution.
CVE-2026-124001.summary_ko: NASA JPL ION-DTN의 DGR 계층에 정수 오버플로 취약점이 있어, 조작된 데이터를 전송해 힙 메모리 손상을 일으키고 서비스 거부나 원격 코드 실행을 유발할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: NASA JPL ION-DTN의 정수 오버플로 취약점으로 힙 메모리 손상 및 원격 코드 실행이나 서비스 거부가 발생할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-125400.description: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in func_pcre() in src/ec_filter.c that reads the PCRE2 ovector after freeing match data. Network-adjacent attackers can send packets matching a loaded pcre_regex() substitution filter to corrupt memory and potentially execute code as root.
CVE-2026-125400.summary_ko: Ettercap에서 필터링 기능 사용 중 메모리 해제 후 참조 문제가 발생합니다. 네트워크 인접 공격자가 조작된 패킷을 보내 메모리를 손상시키고 root 권한으로 코드를 실행할 위험이 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Ettercap의 필터링 기능 중 해제 후 참조(UAF) 취약점이 발생하여 네트워크 인접 공격자가 루트 권한으로 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-125396.description: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a -dSAFER bypass vulnerability in the .putgstringcopy procedure in gs_fonts.ps, which calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking operand types. Attackers can supply crafted PostScript or PDF documents that trigger a type error, recover .forceput via a custom error handler, and cause a use-after-free across save/restore to execute arbitrary code.
CVE-2026-125396.summary_ko: Ghostscript에서 -dSAFER 우회 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 특수하게 제작된 문서로 타입 오류를 유발하여 .forceput 연산자를 호출하고, 이를 통해 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Ghostscript에서 -dSAFER 우회 및 메모리 관리 오류로 임의 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-123815.description: pyLoad is a free and open-source download manager written in Python. Prior to 0.5.0b3.dev102, UnTar._safe_extractall in src/pyload/plugins/extractors/UnTar.py validates archive member paths and link targets but does not call TarInfo.isdev to reject special tar member types before calling tarfile.extractall. On supported Python 3.9 through 3.13 runtimes, tarfile defaults to the fully_trusted extraction filter, so a user with ADD and STATUS permissions can cause extraction of a crafted archive containing character devices, block devices, or FIFOs. Python 3.14 defaults to a safe extraction filter. When pyLoad runs with operating-system privileges that permit device creation, including the official root-based Docker deployment, the archive can expose raw devices and compromise the host. Non-root deployments can still create FIFOs that cause hangs or IPC confusion. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.0b3.dev102.
CVE-2026-123815.summary_ko: pyLoad에서 압축 파일 추출 시 특수 파일 유형에 대한 검증이 부족합니다. 악의적으로 제작된 아카이브를 추출하여 호스트 시스템에 영향을 주거나 장치 파일 생성을 통해 시스템을 침해할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: pyLoad에서 악의적으로 제작된 아카이브 추출 시 특수 장치 파일 생성을 통해 시스템 침해가 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-104989.description: Uncontrolled search path element in package upload feature in Chaos Software V-Ray versions through 2.0.19 allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code via redirecting access to libraries
CVE-2026-104989.summary_ko: Chaos Software V-Ray의 패키지 업로드 기능에 제어되지 않는 검색 경로 요소가 존재하여, 원격의 인증되지 않은 공격자가 라이브러리 접근을 리다이렉트해 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Chaos Software V-Ray의 패키지 업로드 기능 내 경로 탐색으로 원격 인증 없이 임의 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-102643.description: AsyncSSH is a Python package which provides an asynchronous client and server implementation of the SSHv2 protocol on top of the Python asyncio framework. Prior to 2.24.1, SFTPServer.map_path() uses posixpath.normpath() on a client-supplied path and removes only one leading slash before passing the result to posixpath.join() with the configured chroot. An authenticated SFTP user can supply a path beginning with exactly two slash characters, causing POSIX normalization to preserve the double-leading-slash form and the subsequent join to treat the remaining pathname as absolute. This bypasses the SFTP chroot and permits reads and writes with the operating-system permissions of the account running the server, which may enable code execution depending on writable targets. This issue is fixed in version 2.24.1.
CVE-2026-102643.summary_ko: AsyncSSH의 SFTPServer.map_path()에서 경로 처리 오류로 인한 chroot 우회 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 인증된 사용자가 특수 경로를 사용하여 제한된 디렉터리를 벗어나 시스템 파일을 읽거나 쓸 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: AsyncSSH의 SFTP 경로 정규화 미흡으로 chroot 제한을 우회하여 임의 파일 접근이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-84410.description: In apport before 2.37.0, an improper privilege management vulnerability allows an unprivileged local attacker to gain root privileges on systems where automatic crash reporting is enabled. The automatic crash report processing pipeline runs as root and executes ldd on the attacker-controlled ExecutablePath field of a crash file placed in the world-writable /var/crash directory, causing the dynamic loader to load and execute an attacker-supplied audit module specified by the ELF's DT_AUDIT tag. This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges and fully compromise the affected system.

6db771e8455f4eaf46055d8c.title_original: Enhancing Academic Advisement with Case-Based Reasoning
6db771e8455f4eaf46055d8c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This research involved the study of an application of Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) in the field of academic advising. Academic advisement has been recognised as an important function of higher education. However, there is a widespread desire to improve the advisement services provided by many educational institutions (e.g., colleges and universities) around the world. In the last ten years, CBR expert systems have made important contributions in many domains by applying CBR methodology to a variety of areas of human problem solving. However, to date, expert advisement systems have not been successfully applied to academic advisement, which seems to be a very appropriate domain for this technology. Academic advising is an important and time consuming task, and different tools and techniques must be used to make it an effective and efficient process. This thesis describes the design, development, and validation of a prototype case-based academic advisement recommender system that supplements the conventional advising process, and could eventually evolve to replace human academic advisors when its full potential is realised.

2c4ff4e3b19a78045191d2ab.title_original: NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction
2c4ff4e3b19a78045191d2ab.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Normative competence, the ability to infer socially enforced expectations from interaction and adjust behavior accordingly, is essential for agents operating in unfamiliar human communities. Yet existing evaluations largely test whether agents can recognize or apply norms they may already know, rather than whether they can acquire previously unknown norms from social interaction. We introduce NormGym, an interactive benchmark for normative competence in which a newcomer must infer a hidden, arbitrary norm while pursuing its own task in a multi-agent community. Success requires distinguishing what is possible from what is permitted, inferring the norm from observed behavior and sanctions, and applying it in new situations. NormGym contains diverse norms and distinct environments, allowing systematic evaluation of current agents, including large language model (LLM) agents. We find that normative competence remains challenging: the strongest evaluated LLM achieves a joint task-and-compliance success rate of 55.3%. Our analysis reveals that models can sometimes revise their behavior following sanctions for their own actions, but struggle to use other agents' behavior and the sanctions they receive to infer the underlying norm. We further find that fine-tuning models may be insufficient to improve normative competence. These results suggest that current models lack a robust, transferable capability for acquiring normative knowledge

39396743f88d63c1ec88caab.title_original: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
39396743f88d63c1ec88caab.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. This paper proposes an LLM-based feature extraction approach that transforms unstructured sources such as customer reviews into quantitative features using vector embeddings and LLM-generated evaluation criteria. The enriched feature set is incorporated into an MCIC framework based on the Hadi-Vencheh model. Experimental results show measurable reclassification effects when customer sentiment signals are included, demonstrating that integrating unstructured data into MCIC can enhance inventory prioritization.

e6de62fa03391751f6eb8899.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling test-time compute has proven highly effective at improving LLM reasoning. A popular method is best-of-n sampling, where a model generates many candidate solutions and one is selected. This motivates the question: how can we select the best candidate? When humans make choices, we find it more natural to compare two options than judge each in isolation. Additionally, when the options become complex, we like to judge the options one aspect at a time, such as comparing two job candidates on experience, communication, etc. In the test-time setting, candidate solutions should be judged in the same way. Here we introduce Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments (APT), which verifies by comparison and compares by aspect. Each matchup of a single elimination tournament is decided by a vote over multiple off-the-shelf aspect verifiers, each expressing a pairwise preference along its own aspect. Across five domains and three generator LLMs, APT improves over binary multi-aspect approval, self-consistency and reward model verification, with the largest gains on open-ended tasks. We find that both components matter; neither binary approval over the same aspects nor a generic pairwise judge at a matched budget matches APT. Because aspects are specified in natural language, APT also lets users steer selection toward properties they care about, better aligning with user preferences without needing to regenerate solutions. No component is traine

46cb993313cbaeb82f4253ab.title_original: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents
46cb993313cbaeb82f4253ab.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents do not learn from corrections across sessions. A user fixes the same mistake at the start of every conversation. Existing agent memory systems primarily handle facts, such as preferences, entities, and conversational history, rather than procedural knowledge. We present Forge Decision Context (forge_dc), a system that captures behavioral signals from human corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures, compiles them into imperative RULE directives, and injects them at the decision points where they apply. We evaluate forge_dc alongside four predecessor approaches on DC-Bench, a new benchmark of 71 scenarios across nine behavioral dimensions, built from real executed agent traces in a deterministic mocked-tool environment. forge_dc reaches 95% compliance, up from 55% with naive retrieval, while injecting approximately 10 times fewer tokens per query. Across the five-stage progression, the strongest systems represent behavioral memory as explicit directives and deliver it at the decision points where it applies. The results identify representation, activation, and placement as central design choices for persistent behavioral learning.

4d36448083267c67b9640e6a.title_original: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
4d36448083267c67b9640e6a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intra-weight injection lets one model change another model's behaviour by editing its weights directly, without gradients. Such edits can range from altering lexical associations to enforcing output formats or updating factual knowledge. Despite growing interest in these approaches, there has been no systematic way to evaluate how well models perform them. We introduce IWIBench, which measures a large editor model's ability to modify the weights of a smaller target model (typically Gemma 3 4B IT) to achieve one of ten classical text-editing objectives while preserving its other capabilities. Editors are limited to four tools for reading and writing weights, with bounded tensor access and a fixed budget for generating and inspecting rollouts. A validator applies each proposed patch in a clean environment and compares the edited model against the unmodified target. Evaluating frontier closed- and open-weight models reveals sharply diverging capabilities, both across models and across tasks. A small number of models, most notably Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, perform far ahead of the rest. The recency of this ability (little of it is evident in GPT-5.6 Sol, for instance), together with qualitative analysis, suggests it has been acquired through recent training. Tasks also vary widely: structured response resisted every attempt, and answer-length control yielded only one successful solution, whereas alias acquisition and recoding proved mo

7c87daaa57d6162e66f004dd.title_original: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With Pass$_{X}$@$k$
7c87daaa57d6162e66f004dd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive debuggers are indispensable to human software development, yet coding agents overwhelmingly rely on edit-execute-observe loops, using common bash tools, test scripts, and print statements to debug via repeated shell commands. Stepping through a debugger provides live access to runtime state, which may enable different problem-solving capabilities. However, prior work typically introduces the debugger as an additional tool or through a new subagent, making its individual contribution difficult to isolate from the associated scaffold changes. To address this, we compare a debugger-only agent against a bash-only agent on all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, holding the rest of the scaffold fixed. We evaluate both architectures on two models, GPT-OSS-120B and Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B, with three independent runs per architecture $\times$ model configuration. Crucially, to distinguish interface specialization from expanded coverage under repeated sampling, we introduce pass$_X$@$k$, a cross-agent pass@$k$ that provides an unbiased estimator of the probability that at least one of $k$ agents is successful. Although the bash and debugger agents solve partially disjoint subsets of the benchmark in any single pair of runs, our pass$_X$@$2$ estimator reveals that this is largely due to run-to-run variance rather than tool complementarity. Across both models, we find that two bash rollouts outperform the combination of one bash a

d426ac93ddeb5239187598de.title_original: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
d426ac93ddeb5239187598de.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. We introduce ChainFlow, a new speculative decoding paradigm and the first flow-matching drafter conditioned on the target's hidden states. ChainFlow treats drafting as a short transport over hidden states, needing one or two flow steps instead of the many denoising steps of generation from noise. A variational autoencoder compresses these states so drafting cost barely grows with target size, lightweight feedback heads restore inter-token dependencies, and tree drafting raises acceptance. On Qwen3.5 models, at matched drafter size and training data, ChainFlow outperforms EAGLE-3 and DFlash in vLLM by 39% and 11%, respectively. These gains further widen as drafters are adapted to new languages sequentially. Our ablations cover drafter design and concurrent serving, and we open-source our code and drafter models.

703601d48beba6c4e482f366.title_original: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
703601d48beba6c4e482f366.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional. We introduce two complementary frameworks that transport this posterior onto the set of exogenous configurations satisfying a desired counterfactual query. The first constructs a natural pointwise projection and is suitable when the transported exogenous distribution can be used directly. The second enforces mutual independence among counterfactual exogenous variables, so that the transported variables remain interpretable as genuine exogenous noises of the same SCM. We show that both frameworks are consistent with the original backtracking counterfactual principle, and we propose marginal, penalty-based, and hard-constrained solvers for finite-posterior settings. Synthetic experiments on non-bijective SCMs illustrate the geometry of the problem and reveal trade-offs among transport cost, counterfactual constraint satisfaction, and preservation of exogenous independence.

b32e68b57fc685c380bc99d7.title_original: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
b32e68b57fc685c380bc99d7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clients and proxies in front of an LLM engine retry calls that time out. After a transient overload, these retries can keep the engine from recovering even when calls arrive below its capacity. Since the engine may keep computing for clients that have left, propagating cancellation looks like the natural remedy. In this paper, we test it on vLLM with overload experiments on three open models, and with scheduler traces of one that follow each client attempt to the execution it creates in the engine. We find that with retries on, cancellation alone did not restore service in any run, and only 12-38% of the calls that arrived after the overload were delivered. The traces suggest why: retries that vLLM ran typically started prefill less than half a second before they timed out. Executions that vLLM later aborted took 79-85% of the prompt tokens it computed, and vLLM's prompt-token counter missed a third to half of all computed prompt tokens. A retry budget restored service by shedding retries but left many of the overload's calls undelivered. Request coalescing delivered every call from the overload onward, some late, unless cancellation had already aborted the running execution. Overload controls should thus be judged by the executions that retries add and the calls that clients receive.

e3d9713bd78a2878d787f8be.title_original: Memory-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture with LLM-based Orchestration for Conversational Recommendation
e3d9713bd78a2878d787f8be.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational recommender systems often treat user sessions in isolation, limiting their ability to capture how user intent evolves over time. While large language models (LLMs) have improved semantic understanding, they are typically used as isolated components, without addressing how memory, retrieval, and decision-making should be integrated at the system level. In this work, we propose a memory-aware multi-agent architecture for conversational recommendation, in which LLMs act as orchestration layers that coordinate intent refinement, query construction, and interaction flow. A key design principle is the integration of long-term memory as a first-class component, influencing both routing decisions and semantic query formation. We evaluate the system through cross-session memory experiments, multi-turn conversational simulations, and supervisor-driven interaction studies on the Amazon Reviews dataset. Results show that memory-enabled interactions recover up to 63\% of the gap toward explicit-query scenarios and prevent semantic degradation in extended dialogues. In addition, supervisory orchestration increases user acceptance by +28.9 percentage points, highlighting the importance of structured orchestration in guiding interaction and output quality. We also observe an exposure bottleneck between retrieved candidates and displayed recommendations. While LLM-reranking does not improve Hit@K, it consistently enhances semantic

cd14b6c1374e816194980998.title_original: AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference
cd14b6c1374e816194980998.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most LLM architectures have fixed compute demands determined at training time. We propose a novel architecture that combines the Mixture-of-Experts architecture with shallow experts and a novel dynamic-depth system to make the extent of a forward pass dynamically adjustable. Our approach lets the model automatically determine the compute needed for a given task, paired with a system to scale it down after training without retraining when the execution environment demands faster or cheaper inference. To achieve this, we introduce an iterative computation mechanism, sequence-level depth-based routing steered by a halting mechanism within the experts, a depth encoding that lets the model track its progress in the chain, and a regularization mechanism that incentivizes the model to use allocated compute efficiently. We present initial benchmarks and discuss future research directions.

316caec1d382613ca756cb33.title_original: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
316caec1d382613ca756cb33.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, existing approaches typically decouple two inherently related decisions: where to intervene and how to modify the selected components. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optimal intervention location can depend on the intervention applied there, and vice versa. In this work, we introduce AttentionSwitch, the first jailbreak defense to jointly optimize intervention sites and strengths within a frozen LLM. Specifically, AttentionSwitch learns a sparse set of attention heads together with query-conditioned multiplicative scaling factors, allowing the outputs of the selected heads to be either attenuated or amplified without altering the directions of their representations. Across popular language models and jailbreak attacks, AttentionSwitch outperforms existing defenses, with particularly strong results when training data is scarce.

733d8e71f1948b24782f4251.title_original: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
733d8e71f1948b24782f4251.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. Existing approaches -- adversarial suffix/template injection and single-agent self-reflection -- lack robustness across diverse defenses and are prone to confirmation bias and costly trial-and-error, respectively. We propose Debate-to-Deceive (D2D), a multi-agent debate framework grounded in human debate structure and rhetorical style, enabling agents to generate adversarial passages that are semantically coherent, rhetorically effective, and resistant to early confirmation bias. D2D formalizes the adversarial process as an evolutionary game in which agents adaptively evolve their rhetorical strategies (Logos, Pathos, Ethos) through competition. To manage the intractably large LLM output space, we decouple agent behavior into a strategic layer, which selects a rhetorical action from a compact strategy space via evolutionary-inspired learning dynamics, and a generation layer, where the LLM produces a concrete passage conditioned on that strategy and the debate context. On four fact-checking benchmarks (FEVER, HealthVer, CLIMATE-FEVER, and SciFact), D2D substantially outperforms existing attacks and evades most defenses.

61d0334757e152ebe0d4013d.title_original: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
61d0334757e152ebe0d4013d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. We propose Jacobian-causal memory control (JCMC), which represents each authorized memory intervention by a predicted influence signature in a shared behavioral measurement space, selects interventions against a target effect and side-effect budget, and compares predicted with observed effects before retaining or rolling back the intervention. Under explicit smoothness and bounded-estimation assumptions, we prove a quadratic local-approximation bound, characterize the target effects reachable by a set of signatures, bound selection regret under signature error, and bound non-additive interactions between simultaneous memories. The paper reports no benchmark measurements; it defines a paired counterfactual estimator and an evaluation protocol comparing JCMC with relevance, graph, and policy-filtered retrieval baselines. The central claim is narrowed or falsified if those simpler baselines match effect targeting, side-effect control, and rollback utility under equal model, memory, policy, and cost budgets.

d22ec9f1b85be2bdf48e492c.title_original: Aligning, Fast and Slow: A Control-Theoretic Oversight Framework for Long-Horizon Trajectories and Maintained Deployments
d22ec9f1b85be2bdf48e492c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can pass checks on individual tasks while retaining memory or code changes that alter their later behavior. We introduce a control-theoretic framework that couples a fast loop controlling proposed actions with a slow loop reviewing persistent changes and reassessing configurations after model or tool updates. When measurement errors and changes between checks are bounded and controllers can enforce their decisions, we derive a deployment-level bound and a rule for dividing review effort. In simulation, dividing a fixed review budget between both loops reduces mean maximum departure from intended behavior roughly twelvefold compared with review confined to individual runs. In coding stress tests with authored memories and five matched seeds, combined controls reduce mean severity on a 0-3 scale from 0.325 without gates to 0.117, resolving 33 of 120 issues versus 35 without gates; in trading stress tests, combined controls reduce mean shortfall in low-emission purchases from 0.892 without gates to 0.107. The overall framework helps developers and auditors compare and enforce oversight designs, while the agent studies test component controls rather than the full deployment-level guarantee.

200714866b294e8b53577cd3.title_original: The Matthews Correlation Coefficient: Fifty years
200714866b294e8b53577cd3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fifty years after its introduction, the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) remains central -and debated- in binary classification. This survey offers a comprehensive retrospective and an in-depth analysis of MCC, covering its historical development, mathematical foundations, and implications for practice. We clarify long-standing misconceptions, formalize its equivalences (to Pearson's correlation and to Chi2 in 2x2 tables), and examine its behavior under class imbalance. Beyond MCC, we develop analytical (derivatives) and graphical (contour plots) frameworks that generalize to any confusion-matrix-based metric. These frameworks expose structural properties -bias, robustness, sensitivity- that scalar summaries conceal, and they provide actionable guidance for selecting and interpreting performance measures in applications where reliability and fairness matter. Together, our results position MCC within a broader toolkit while clarifying when it is informative -and when alternatives may be preferable.

363d7e8b4d21d2d17a4bbd4b.title_original: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
363d7e8b4d21d2d17a4bbd4b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) are one of the key components of current agentic systems. LRMs augment their output with an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning stage, introducing a new attack surface for thought injection, in which untrusted text resembling the model's own deliberation is fed back to the model. We present a two-part study of this attack, performed against the prevailing large, production class open-weight models (e.g., GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.5, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). We first evaluate the effectiveness of static thought-injection prompts under different styles as well as tagged and untagged conditions and find that the effects of thinking tags and payload styles are all properties of the specific target model. In the second study, we exploit this model-specificity in a containerized agentic cyber range, using indirect injection prompts styled in the form of the target model's own reasoning traces to achieve attack success rates (ASR) up to 50% on operational objectives such as reverse-shell exfiltration and repository backdooring. We also find that the same malicious objective in standard prompt injection user voice never succeeds, and thinking tags suppress the agent's tendency to disclose the injection. Our results show that imitating a reasoning model's own thought style is effective for this style of attack, and that tag stripping is an unreliable defense.

e30e411d3f57ccec8124123e.title_original: Notwithstanding Anything to the Contrary, Ignore All Instructions: Measuring Prompt Injection Guards on Legal Contract Review Attacks
